landing.headline: On the frontier between strategy and execution.
landing.summary: I lead results-focused decisions, combining financial rigor, data and business context, from setting the strategy to executing it.
landing.impactLink: See the full impact timeline in Career →
landing.ctaBody: Open to challenges where strategy and execution must move together.

whoIAm.resumo: I've spent the past decade on the frontier between strategy and execution: the work of making complex decisions clear, funded, and, above all, executed. An economist from UNICAMP, I began in Finance at Bosch and Serasa Experian and built a track record leading FP&A and Strategy at digital-first companies and marketplaces. Today I'm part of Landa Club Cohort 20, a community of entrepreneurs and consultants focused on technology and new business in Latin America, and a certified board director through Board Academy, ready to contribute on boards, including more junior seats.
whoIAm.value: I connect strategy and execution: turning analysis into decision, and decision into coordinated movement across teams. My edge is no longer in producing the number. It's in asking the right question, providing the business context, and uniting teams around the decision. With AI taking on much of the analysis, my value concentrates in that judgment and orchestration.
whoIAm.think: I structure problems by Fact, Cause and Action, and prioritize by reach, importance, and effort. The full mental model, with the frameworks for data, AI, presentation, and governance, is in How I Think.
whoIAm.thinkLink: See the full mental model in How I Think →
whoIAm.seek: Digital-first companies in growth, including those going through transformation under PE/VC, where strategy and execution must move together: growing with governance, innovating with control, scaling without losing predictability. It's the context where a Planning and Strategy function stops being support and becomes the axis that sustains growth.

inflection.title: Four moments that changed how I operate.
inflection.intro: Not only successes, but evolution. This is probably the most personal page on the site: four moments when a belief I held about my craft was confronted by reality and had to change.
inflection.m1Title: Leaving iFood to build at Porto
inflection.m1Believed: I believed that building mattered more than controlling, and that accelerated growth, on its own, was the main driver of valuation. Controls and resource discipline felt secondary next to speed.
inflection.m1Happened: With the end of the era of "artificially cheap capital" after the pandemic, the cost of money rose and startups and scale-ups were forced to rethink their growth models, now under pressure to show efficiency, not just expansion.
inflection.m1Changed: The market began demanding ambidexterity: growing and innovating without giving up control and efficient use of resources. I saw that one doesn't live without the other.
inflection.m1Today: I practice ambidextrous management: I use innovation to raise the company's ceiling, gaining scale and scope, and pair it with continuous control and efficiency, which generate the profitability needed to fund the very efforts of expansion and innovation.
inflection.m2Believed: I saw Finance, above all, as an area to fuel growth. That, to me, was its main value proposition.
inflection.m2Happened: We had to abruptly shrink the Olho Mágico operation. The sharp rise in interest rates and the end of Porto's (PSSA3) Corporate Capital risk appetite for the venture made the scenario unsustainable.
inflection.m2Changed: The radical shift in funding availability and the steep drop in runway forced the downsizing and the layoff of 20 people. Handling that while keeping respect and clarity with those leaving and those staying was one of the hardest decisions of my career.
inflection.m2Today: I learned that Finance is not only support for growth and innovation: it is also risk management and work with medium- and long-term scenarios. And that hard conversations are part of the seat; avoiding them costs more than facing them.
inflection.m3Believed: I saw governance as a process restricted to internal controls, procurement, accounting, and controllership. I didn't see FP&A at the center of that conversation.
inflection.m3Happened: I had to run a due diligence for Warburg Pincus's evaluation to acquire VOLL, which put the quality and traceability of the financial numbers under external scrutiny.
inflection.m3Changed: FP&A became central: both in gathering the governance documentation and in structuring the processes that sustain it, such as management by indicators, revenue and cost audit controls, and predictability ensured by the accuracy of the numbers.
inflection.m3Today: I constantly assess whether the chosen KPIs really move the business, and whether they are accurate, reliable, and predictable. That, together with clear, transparent governance of results and forecast data, is what gives the confidence to decide quickly.
inflection.m4Title: AI and the value of my own work
inflection.m4Believed: I grew professionally by producing good analyses, cross-referencing data, and generating actionable insights. I believed it was exactly that, the quality of my own analysis, that defined my value.
inflection.m4Happened: I found that AI does this better than I do, and faster. Acknowledging that openly is a real vulnerability: what got me here is no longer a guarantee of anything.
inflection.m4Changed: Instead of fighting AI, I began using it at full power, because that is value, not a threat. My focus shifted to what the machine doesn't do: uniting teams, managing priorities, and ensuring the best decisions turn into value for the company.
inflection.m4Today: I use AI as a multiplier and concentrate my value in judgment, context, and people. And I lead teams to use more AI, be more productive, and walk the same development path I did.

howIThink.title: The reasoning behind the results.
howIThink.intro: Career tells what happened; here I tell the reasoning behind it.
howIThink.a1Anchor: Turnaround at Rappi · downsizing at Porto
howIThink.a1Lead: Priority is reach, importance and effort, weighed at the right level.
howIThink.a1b1: Reach (scope it touches), importance (result it moves), effort (resources it takes).
howIThink.a1b2: More weight when the impact is at the company level, not just my area.
howIThink.a1b3: Top: high reach with proportional effort. The urgent never hijacks the essential.
howIThink.a2Anchor: OKRs + FCA management · iFood and Decolar
howIThink.a2Lead: Fact, Cause and Action: it moves decisions from opinion to what can be measured.
howIThink.a2b1: Fact: an unquestionable, measured data point, never a perception.
howIThink.a2b2: Cause: the real root I'm responsible to act on, never an external one.
howIThink.a2b3: Action: measurable and tied directly to the Fact's indicator.
howIThink.a3Title: How I turn data into decisions
howIThink.a3Anchor: ABCD matrix at Serasa · dashboards at VOLL
howIThink.a3Lead: From reliable data to the message that decides.
howIThink.a3b1: A single source of truth (OSST); if it doesn't exist, I build it.
howIThink.a3b2: I separate signal from noise and answer one objective business question.
howIThink.a3b3: I close with a visualization carrying ONE clear message, in the decider's language.
howIThink.a4Anchor: AI adoption at Decolar (Toqan, Claude Code)
howIThink.a4Lead: AI as a multiplier, with judgment always mine.
howIThink.a4b1: Automate: repetitive, low-risk tasks that are easy to validate.
howIThink.a4b2: Analyze: recurring routines over reliable pipelines, pre-agreed with the users.
howIThink.a4b3: Complex: skills that adapt AI to each business context.
howIThink.a5Anchor: Localiza and Despegar boards · Rappi HQ
howIThink.a5b1: Purpose: explain the past, project scenarios, or unlock a decision?
howIThink.a5b2: The audience's framework: financial, problem-solving, or collaborative?
howIThink.a5b3: Stakeholders: what I expect from each, with deadline and tone. Lead to the decision, don't just show data.
howIThink.a6Title: How I balance speed and governance
howIThink.a6Anchor: Innovation with control · iFood and Decolar
howIThink.a6Lead: Holes in the ship, yes; below the waterline, never.
howIThink.a6b1: I define where control is non-negotiable and where failing fast is welcome.
howIThink.a6b2: I keep the team in the OK zone: bureaucracy doesn't kill innovation, lack of process doesn't cause misalignment.

career.title: A trajectory on the frontier between strategy and execution.
career.intro: Six companies. The impact first, then the story behind each one.
career.timelineNote: * 2026 figures are estimated. Values in USD at a fixed rate (R$5 = US$1). Data provided by Heitor Mobílio.
career.decolarContext: Brazil's leading OTA, post-acquisition by the Prosus group, amid a culture shift and growth acceleration.
career.decolarChallenge: Establish Planning and Strategy governance and the management model for the Brazil B2C P&L to sustain growth and secure the strategic transition.
career.decolarActions: Restructured the team under the Prosus culture, consolidated the management model by reworking the strategy-execution rituals, accelerated AI adoption, and consolidated the reporting pack to the Despegar board.
career.decolarImpact: New management rituals in place, with OKRs aligned to growth targets; recognized as the sponsor of the AI agenda in Brazil.
career.decolarLessons: Expanding Finance into strategy demands excellence in reporting fundamentals, even under shifting leadership and culture. First earn trust through technical depth, then expand the impact.
career.vollContext: B2B traveltech (Localiza group) in rapid expansion, with +40% in three months, demanding financial governance.
career.vollChallenge: Build reliable governance and forecasting to sustain growth without Finance being a bottleneck, amid team seniority upgrades and an ERP migration.
career.vollActions: Built post-ERP revenue-data auditing through quality dashboards, weekly business tracking, and pipeline management; analyzed the largest costs to protect gross margin.
career.vollImpact: EBITDA forecast accuracy from 80% to 98% and revenue from 89% to 99%; led the due diligence for Warburg Pincus's purchase of the L&Co stake.
career.vollLessons: Reliability and predictability, paired with clear, transparent governance, are the scaffolding of healthy accelerated growth.
career.vollEvidence: Recommendation from Mirna A. Carvalho (CFO). See Recommendations.
career.rappiContext: Delivery marketplace with a recent Box Delivery acquisition, betting on a new logistics model to gain market share.
career.rappiChallenge: Grow with austerity: capture Box Delivery synergies and reduce the Brazil operation's burn against an established leader.
career.rappiActions: Led the turnaround across every area, as the conductor of the joint effort to deliver the result; created Box Delivery↔Rappi logistics-integration forums and weekly decision rituals.
career.rappiImpact: Brazil operation to breakeven in 9 months, recognized by the Brazil CEO within 3 months; Box Delivery unit delivery cost at ~70% of the average.
career.rappiLessons: Structural course-correction, paired with growth and efficiency, is as central in times of adjustment as in times of growth.
career.rappiEvidence: Recommendations from Mirna A. Carvalho and Luiz Otávio Giordani Junior. See Recommendations.
career.portoContext: A digital venture (Olho Mágico) inside Porto (PSSA3) to enter the real-estate rental and sales market.
career.portoChallenge: Build a digital product inside a market-leading incumbent, an ambidexterity demand, then navigate the hardening macro environment.
career.portoActions: Led the Finance and Data Analytics team, built a multidisciplinary team, and integrated NIDO Tecnologia post-M&A; ran the downsizing when viability proved unsustainable.
career.portoImpact: Built the Olho Mágico brand, with a listings portal matching the market leader's size in just 8 months; successful NIDO integration despite the adverse context.
career.portoLessons: A first major leadership role and direct responsibility for the finances of a strategic venture in a listed group brought maturity in negotiation, executive presentation, and hard decisions.
career.ifoodContext: First digital-native, mobile-first company, with direct exposure to OKR management and results-driven decisions.
career.ifoodChallenge: First leadership role, amid the pandemic, needing to structure the financial viability of marketing and new products.
career.ifoodActions: Led restaurant relief during COVID-19, managed exclusivity contracts, optimized performance marketing in the weekly agenda with the CMO, and structured iFood Clube.
career.ifoodImpact: R$1bn+ injected into the cash flow of 45k+ restaurants; the financial backbone of iFood Clube, today 90% of food-delivery marketing spend; pioneered LTV/CAC.
career.ifoodLessons: Agile, precise financial management in the New Economy, results-driven leadership, and structuring strategic projects.
career.ifoodEvidence: Recommendations from Paula Cabianca and Carolina Rodrigues. See Recommendations.
career.serasaContext: A consolidated market leader in financial information, but with little efficiency analysis in Sales and Marketing.
career.serasaChallenge: First experience in Finance: build the FP&A toolkit and deliver results through strong relationships.
career.serasaActions: Built sales-pipeline and efficiency analyses with an ABCD matrix (new revenue vs. investment) and rationalized Marketing and Events spend.
career.serasaImpact: Better capital allocation in the sales team, with the pipeline managed weekly by the VP; savings in Marketing and Events.
career.serasaLessons: Analyses that drive leadership action. The recognition that took me, by referral, to iFood.
